findings.description: The new scrubber checks executable destinations without normalizing path components. `.git/objects/../hooks/pre-commit` therefore misses the `.git/hooks` rule and is classified as a plain file.
findings.failure_mode: With an existing executable pre-commit hook, `tee .git/objects/../hooks/pre-commit <<'EOF'\nif true; then rm -rf /; fi\nEOF` overwrites that hook while preserving its executable permission. The body scanner drops all three segments because their first words are `if`, `then`, and `fi`, so the destructive command disappears before fence matching. A subsequent commit executes the hook. Previously, the quoted-cat-only scrub did not remove this tee body.
findings.suggested_fix: Normalize destination paths before testing executable locations, resolving existing parent directories and symlinks. Fall back to scanning the complete body whenever destination resolution fails.

findings.description: check_implement_marker is called as a bare statement, and its 1 or 2 return code is then read with marker_rc=$?. If the hook, or anything it sources, enables errexit, the absent marker case (rc 1) and the stale marker case (rc 2) end the script right there. No ask, deny or audit row is emitted.
findings.failure_mode: Under set -e the hook exits with status 1 on every unsanctioned App Zone write that has no marker. Claude Code treats exit 1 as a non-blocking hook error and lets the write through. In deny mode the gate then fails open and writes no telemetry row.
findings.suggested_fix: Capture the code in a way errexit cannot interrupt: `marker_rc=0; check_implement_marker || marker_rc=$?`.

findings.description: The implement-active marker only sanctions writes while started_at is less than 7200 seconds old. Nothing in this diff refreshes started_at during a long /implement or /bug session. When there is no RUNNING sprint-plan cache, a session longer than two hours loses its sanction partway through.
findings.failure_mode: In ask mode the session starts prompting on every App Zone write once two hours have passed, which stalls autonomous runs. In deny mode with a fresh derived cache that is not RUNNING, every later write is denied, so the in-progress implementation fails.
findings.suggested_fix: Refresh started_at on each checkpoint or task boundary. Alternatively, key freshness to a last_activity field and keep the 2h window as a staleness bound measured from the last refresh.

findings.description: check_implementation_active now also requires derived_at to fall within run_mode.stale_hours, which defaults to 12. It used to require only a RUNNING state and a last_activity under 24h old. A run whose cache is not re-derived at least every 12h, while activity stays fresh, now stops counting as sanctioned.
findings.failure_mode: During a long sprint-plan run that does not re-derive often, App Zone writes switch from allowed to ask in the default mode, or to deny under deny mode. Previously these writes were allowed. This is a silent regression for run-mode.
findings.suggested_fix: Make sure every run-checkpoint activity update also rewrites derived_at, or apply the derived_at bound only in deny mode. Add a bats case for a RUNNING cache with fresh activity and a 13h-old derived_at.

findings.cross_file_justification: The result now comes entirely from loa_knob in .claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh, which this diff changes but does not show. Its behavior when yq is missing or the config is malformed decides whether enforcement fails open.
findings.description: Before this change, a missing config file, a missing yq or a yq error all resolved to enforcement ON. Now everything goes through loa_knob with fallback false. If profile-lib cannot read the config, for example because yq is missing, an operator's explicit `guardrails.danger_level.enforce: true` resolves to false.
findings.failure_mode: The danger-level safety control silently turns off on hosts without yq or with a config that does not parse, even when the operator explicitly enabled it. The same regression applies to the input guardrails include, which now needs the knob to print true.
findings.suggested_fix: Tell 'key absent' apart from 'config unreadable'. When the config exists but loa_knob cannot evaluate it, fail closed and enforce. Add a bats case for explicit enforce:true with no yq on PATH.

findings.cross_file_justification: The include tells the model to run .claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh with a `knob` subcommand. That only works if the truncated profile-lib.sh is executable and has a CLI dispatcher. retrospective_postlude.md calls the same CLI without a fallback argument.
findings.description: Before, guardrails ran unless they were explicitly disabled. Now they run only when the knob CLI prints `true`. If the lib is not executable, needs a fallback argument, or exits early, it prints nothing. The skill then skips guardrails even with an explicit `enabled: true` or the full profile. The two includes also call the CLI inconsistently: one passes a fallback and the other does not.
findings.failure_mode: Input guardrails, and possibly the retrospective, are skipped without any error when the knob CLI fails. An operator who opted in gets no protection and no signal.
findings.suggested_fix: Confirm profile-lib.sh is executable and that `knob KEY [FALLBACK]` works with and without a fallback. Add a test that runs both include command lines verbatim. Consider failing closed for guardrails when the CLI errors.

findings.description: In loa-kf-surface.sh and loa-decisions-surface.sh, `enabled` is assigned only when sourcing profile-lib succeeds. The l6 and l7 hooks in the same diff initialize `enabled="false"` first, but these two do not. If the source fails, `enabled` keeps whatever value it had before, or stays unset.
findings.failure_mode: Under set -u, an unset `enabled` aborts the session-start hook. If the variable was pre-set or inherited, the surface may run or be suppressed against the config. Sourcing the lib can also change the hook's shell options.
findings.suggested_fix: Initialize `enabled="false"` before the source line in both hooks, matching loa-l6-surface-handoffs.sh.

findings.description: The exported library entry point _bdb_heredoc_consumer_class sets LC_ALL=C before classifying. The hook's own call site runs _bdb_heredoc_scrub directly under the user's locale. Bracket ranges like [A-Za-z] in the delimiter, control-character and flag regexes, and character-indexed substring walks in the tokenizer can behave differently in UTF-8 locales.
findings.failure_mode: The corpus tests and heredoc-classifier.sh consumers go through the library and can get a different classification than the live hook for the same command. That makes the fail-closed guarantees hard to rely on, and tokenizing long headers costs quadratic time in multibyte locales.
findings.suggested_fix: Run the hook's scrub under the same locale, for example in a function that declares `local LC_ALL=C`, so the tests and production share one code path.

findings.description: The knob reader only recognizes block-style YAML with heredoc_classifier on an indented line under `destructive_command_guard:`. A flow-style mapping, a quoted top-level key, or anchors and merges are not seen, and the classifier stays on.
findings.failure_mode: An operator who turns the looser classifier off with valid YAML the reader does not parse still gets the classifier. Turning it off is the tightening direction, so that setting is silently ignored.
findings.suggested_fix: Read the key with yq when it is available and keep the line scanner only as the fallback. Otherwise, document and lint that only block style is supported.

findings.cross_file_justification: The diff removes C-TEAM-001 through C-TEAM-005 and the generated Agent Teams table in CLAUDE.loa.md. Truncated files such as agent-teams-reference.md, generate-constraints.sh, validate-constraints.sh and lint-invariants.sh, along with hook messages, may still cite these IDs or the agent_teams_constraints section.
findings.description: The always-loaded instruction rules for teammates are removed. These rules serialized beads operations, git commit and push, and .run state writes through the lead. Only some of them, such as team-skill-guard and the System Zone write hook, have mechanical enforcement. The rest now exist only in an on-demand reference doc, if anywhere.
findings.failure_mode: In Agent Teams sessions, teammates are no longer told in-context not to run br or git commit concurrently. That brings back the SQLite lock contention and index.lock races these constraints came from in incident #337. Any validator or doc still citing C-TEAM IDs points at constraints that no longer exist.
findings.suggested_fix: Confirm agent-teams-reference.md keeps these rules and is loaded whenever TeamCreate is used. Grep for any remaining C-TEAM-00x references and agent_teams_constraints markers so generation and validation do not drift.
